secrets.name: apiKey
secrets.description: TypeSafe API key used only for POST requests to api.typesafe.ai

tools.name: classify
tools.description: Triage, sort, or label many emails, messages, receipts, files, or photos with Jev, a fast decision model. Use it for 15 or more items, for items saved as files or images, or when you need each label's probability. Pass saved items as paths, with `files` or an item's `file`. Returns each item's label, every label's probability, Jev's confidence, and `uncertain` when the label's probability is under 0.5. Every label set also offers "none of these". Example uses: emails into urgent/reply/newsletter/junk, receipts into business/personal, photos into contains-passport/other.

items.description: The items, in order. Results name each item by its id, its file path, or its 1-based position.
An item as text, or an object with text, a text file, or an image, plus an optional id.

id.description: A name for the item that results use, such as an email subject or a listing URL.

file.description: Path to a text file holding the item, such as a saved email or a note.

image.description: Path to a PNG or JPEG image of the item.

files.description: Paths or glob patterns, such as "inbox/*.eml". Each matched file becomes one item named by its path; PNG and JPEG files are read as images, others as text.

labels.description: The labels to choose from. Give each a short description of what belongs in it.

description.description: What an item needs to get this label.

instructions.description: What to judge about each item, such as "by what the user needs to do with it".

context.description: Background every item is judged against, such as the user's preferences or situation.

keep.description: Label names to return; other items are counted under `omitted`. Use it to keep only the urgent emails, for example.

tools.name: rank
tools.description: Rank, shortlist, or prioritize many options, such as apartments, offers, tasks, or photos, by a criterion with Jev, a fast decision model. Use it for 15 or more items, for items saved as files or images, or when you need a score per item. Pass saved items as paths, with `files` or an item's `file`. Returns the items best first, each with a 0-1 score, the nearest level on the scale, and Jev's confidence. Example uses: apartments, job offers, restaurants, tasks by importance, photos by quality.

items.description: The items, in order. Results name each item by its id, its file path, or its 1-based position.
An item as text, or an object with text, a text file, or an image, plus an optional id.

id.description: A name for the item that results use, such as an email subject or a listing URL.

file.description: Path to a text file holding the item, such as a saved email or a note.

image.description: Path to a PNG or JPEG image of the item.

files.description: Paths or glob patterns, such as "inbox/*.eml". Each matched file becomes one item named by its path; PNG and JPEG files are read as images, others as text.

criterion.description: What makes an item better, stated concretely, such as "fits a family of 4, under 2000 EUR a month, near a metro".

levels.description: Optional scale from worst to best, 2 to 10 level names. Defaults to poor fit, weak fit, partial fit, good fit, excellent fit.

context.description: Background every item is judged against, such as the user's preferences or situation.

top.description: How many of the best items to return; the rest are counted under `omitted`.
